requirement: Limit each client to five requests per sixty-second window through a dependency, answering 429 with a Retry-After header rounded up to whole seconds once the window is spent, reporting remaining requests on admitted calls and requiring a client id header.
skeleton: LIMIT, WINDOW and an injectable clock, a FixedWindow class validating its settings and returning remaining and retry-after per hit, a module LIMITER with reset_db, a rate_limited dependency reading X-Client-Id, and a GET /search handler.
caption: Rate limiting a FastAPI endpoint with a fixed window. LIMIT is 5 and WINDOW is 60 seconds; clock() reads NOW so tests can move time. FixedWindow(limit, window) raises ValueError saying limit and window must be positive when either is below one, and keeps a (window start, count) pair per key. hit(key, now) starts a fresh window once at least window seconds have passed; if the count already equals the limit it returns zero remaining and a retry delay of math.ceil of the seconds until the window ends, never less than one, otherwise it stores the incremented count and returns how many remain with delay zero. rate_limited(response, x_client_id) raises HTTPException 400 saying the X-Client-Id header is required when it is missing, calls LIMITER.hit, raises HTTPException 429 saying rate limit exceeded with a Retry-After header when the delay is positive, and otherwise sets X-RateLimit-Remaining. GET /search depends on it through Annotated Depends. The fixture asserts five admitted calls with remaining 4 down to 0, a sixth call 12.2 seconds later answering 429 with Retry-After 48, a new window exactly 60 seconds later, separate counts per client, 400 without the header, and ValueError for a zero limit.

plan.intent: Protect search from bursts by any single client
constraints: At most LIMIT requests per client per WINDOW seconds
Excess requests raise HTTPException 429 with Retry-After rounded up
A new window starts once WINDOW seconds have passed

rationale.teaches: A dependency that counts per key in fixed windows, returns 429 with a ceiling-rounded Retry-After, and reports remaining quota.
rationale.why: Off-by-one window and limit comparisons, truncated retry delays and a counter shared across clients all pass a single-client smoke test, so the fixture walks the exact boundaries with a controllable clock.

ops.docstring: Per-client fixed-window rate limiting that tells callers when to retry.

ops.stmt: from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Header, HTTPException, Response, status

candidates.why_wrong: The window only resets after strictly more than WINDOW seconds, so a client is blocked one tick too long.
int truncates the delay, so clients retry a second early and are rejected again.
Every client shares one counter, so one busy client blocks everyone else.
The 429 response omits Retry-After, so clients cannot know when to try again.
The limit comparison lets a sixth request through each window.
